messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: model-infer-v3 -> traffic 15% in prod-us, id=clr-1955

sara.chen: seeing a jump in 5xx from the canary hosts, 503s and timeouts across /v1/generate. started ~10:02 UTC

michael_oncall: paging in. oncall here, looking. which hosts?

sara.chen: canary hosts: infer-canary-3a, infer-canary-3b. error rate ~12% at 10:03. p95 latency doubled. logs show repeated kv-cache misses + OOM-ish GC spikes.

incident-bot: @michael_oncall @eng-release incident created: INC-1955 (unwind requested) — severity: high — channel: #incidents

eng-release: tagging — we pushed a quantized kernel layer plus a config change to memory pool (optimize-kv=true). suspect new kernel regression.

michael_oncall: ok. automated rollback didn't trigger (threshold was 20% and probe window 5m). We need a manual unwind. Can someone prepare the traffic-shift commands?

ops-bot: suggested command: `redwoodctl route shift --service infer-prod --from model-infer-v3 --to model-infer-v2 --pct 100 --grace 30s`

kavita.s: I can run manual shift. Will also disable the feature flag `enable-quant-kernel-v3` in case traffic shift leaves residual state.

jamie_prod: customer impact? any customers paged?

sara.chen: early estimate: ~0.9% of requests in 3 regions received 5xx between 10:02-10:12. Some PLG users saw degraded responses; we have 12 confirmed support tickets from high-touch accounts.

michael_oncall: running `redwoodctl route shift` now. output:

```
> redwoodctl route shift --service infer-prod --from model-infer-v3 --to model-infer-v2 --pct 100 --grace 30s
Shifting traffic... 25% -> 50% -> 100% complete
Completed at 10:08 UTC
```

sara.chen: monitoring metrics... error rate dropping. p95 latency falling back toward baseline.

kavita.s: feature flag `enable-quant-kernel-v3` disabled across prod. confirm: `ffctl get enable-quant-kernel-v3` -> `false`

ops-bot: also cleaned up canary pods: `kubectl -n prod delete pod infer-canary-3a infer-canary-3b` (they were stuck in CrashLoopBackOff)

michael_oncall: quick smoke: run `curl -sS -X POST https://infer.prod/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'` and assert 200. kavita, can you run a few across regions?

kavita.s: ran in us-east/us-west/eu-west. all returned 200, median latency 210ms.

eng-release: digging into logs from the canary: kernel v3 uses a different allocator that seems to fragment under the request shape we push. reproducer in staging with a short-sequence workload causes increments in `kv_cache_alloc` leading to GC pressure. attaching snippet:

```
[10:03:05] kv_cache_alloc: +1.2MB
[10:03:06] mem_pressure: high
[10:03:07] eviction: triggered
[10:03:07] error: allocation failed
```

jamie_prod: thanks. customers: notifying SRE and CS teams. I'll coordinate messaging. timeline for full recovery?

michael_oncall: services back to baseline at ~10:10 UTC. closing the immediate on-call loop. handoff to oncall-next for postmortem and follow-up at 10:18.

incident-bot: @jamie_prod assigned owner=customer-comms, @kavita.s assigned owner=validation, @eng-release assigned owner=bugfix.

eng-release: plan: revert quant-kernel v3 change from canary, add safety breaker to auto-disable kernel if mem_pressure > 80% for 60s, and add a tighter canary alert (10% errors in 2m). will target patch in next patch release.

kavita.s: verification steps we ran:
- traffic shift to stable
- disable flag
- delete canary pods
- smoke requests across regions (status, latency)
- check rollout metrics for 15m post unwind

michael_oncall: logging summary for handoff:
- incident start: 1955556789 (10:02 UTC)
- mitigation: manual traffic shift to model-infer-v2 at 10:08 UTC
- mitigation: disabled feature flag at 10:09 UTC
- recovery observed: 10:10 UTC metrics normalized
- duration: ~8 minutes of elevated errors
- customer impact: limited, PLG minor degradations, 12 support tickets, no data loss

jamie_prod: taking post-incident owning. next steps for postmortem: root cause analysis, fix + rollback safety, runbook update for canary exits, customer communication draft. I'll schedule a postmortem meeting for tomorrow.

eng-release: adding these action items to the release checklist: 1) disable quant-kernel by default behind a stricter flag, 2) reduce automated-rollback thresholds to 10% error over 2m, 3) add memory-pressure probe that triggers safe-exit.

ops-bot: logged runbook edits: `docs/runbooks/canary-unwind.md` (todo: add exact commands we used today and amplify the `redwoodctl` examples).

incident-bot: Incident INC-1955 status: resolved -> monitoring. responders: michael_oncall, sara.chen, kavita.s, eng-release, jamie_prod.

michael_oncall: handing off to @jamie_prod for postmortem and to next oncall for follow-up. if anything regresses ping me.

jamie_prod: noted. will post summary for customers and assign follow-ups. thanks all for quick coordination :thumbsup:
